text:
sam: noticed a steady climb in OOMs on eu-west yesterday around 11:07 UTC, started during the promo spike :chart_with_upwards_trend:

mira: saw that — Prometheus alerts showed GPU memory pressure rising well before request LB errors. logs attached in infra-s3.

jon: timeline we have so far: 11:02 traffic ramp begins, 11:05 autoscaler starts spinning up new pods, 11:06 kube-scheduler latencies spike, 11:07 a subset of pods hit near-oom and restarted.

lia: key thing: these were long-chat requests (seq len ~12k tokens) pinned to dedicated-pool-eu2 due to routing policy. prefix caching didn't trigger because sessions were new.

sam: correct — and we had a network hiccup between nodes that increased RPC latency to storage for KV cache, so runtime kept larger KV caches per-request and couldn't free them fast enough.

mira: ops-bot posted the earlier automated alert: "GPU_MEMORY_HIGH on node-euw2-12 (93%)" at 11:06:42.

ops-bot: Incident note: autoscaler cooldown was 120s, minNodes=2, maxNodes=18, scaleAttempts=3. Backoff started after repeated scheduling failures.

jon: root causes (draft): 1) long-tail sequence distribution during promo = higher peak memory per inference; 2) transient network storage latency causing KV cache retention; 3) autoscaler cooldown and scheduler queueing delayed capacity reaction; 4) routing policy pinned to dedicated pool with limited spare headroom.

lia: immediate mitigations we applied: started a manual scale of dedicated-pool-eu2 (+4 GPUs) at 11:09, rolled a hotfix to reduce per-request KV cache retention to 30s at 11:12, and enabled fallback routing to hosted-model-b at 11:15.

sam: consequence: ~7% of requests experienced 500/oom errors for 6 minutes, tail latency doubled for 3% of requests. Cost delta: extra 4 GPUs for ~40 minutes = ~160 GPU-minutes (~2.7 GPU-hours). Will pull billing detail.

mira: patch note: the retention change was a config tweak in runtime flags: ```--kv-cache-retention=30s``` — safer default for high-churn workloads. We reverted staged increase of retention we had deployed two weeks ago.

jon: on autoscaler: cooldown=120s felt too long for sudden promos. Proposal: add burst mode where we temporarily set cooldown=20s if traffic slope > 15%/m and headroom < 10%. Thoughts?

lia: agree. Add a safety cap to avoid thrash: allow at most +25% nodes burst above target for 15m and then evaluate. Also mark a metric to prefer adding smaller instances first (1 GPU increments) to reduce overshoot.

sam: networking angle — needs postmortem with infra-net: packet drops between nodes caused gRPC timeouts to the KV backend. @mira can you loop in neteng and attach tcpdump windows?

mira: will do. early capture shows spikes in retransmits at 11:05-11:08 on eth1 of node-euw2-10. I put pcap in /infra/pcaps/euw2/1802500000.pcap.

ops-bot: NOTE: deploy-bot recorded a config rollout 10:55 UTC to change kernel tunables for hugepages on dedicated-pool-eu2. ChangeID: DPL-2026. Investigating correlation.

jon: ops thought: we shouldn't have both kernel tunable changes and retention increases landing before a high-traffic window. Need stricter coordination for infra changes during promotions.

lia: forecasting lesson: our capacity model underweighted long-chat tail by ~3x during peak. We assume median seqlen but promo uses many multi-turn flows. Need to add a tail multiplier and re-evaluate headroom for promo windows.

sam: quick actions list (assigned): mira -> neteng ticket + pcaps; jon -> autoscaler burst PR and tests; lia -> capacity model update and run what-if for next promo; mira -> billing export for cost delta; sam -> postmortem writeup and stakeholder note.

mira: will also add a short-term rule to route long-chats to hosted fallback when dedicated headroom < 15% to avoid OOMs.

sam: timeline update: all mitigations reduced errors by 11:21 and normal routing resumed at 11:30. final customer impact window ~11:06-11:21.

jon: long-term items: add pre-promotions runbook (scale plan, disable risky infra changes, extra monitoring for KV latency), add probe synthetic long-chat workload to staging, and add an autoscaler simulation harness.

lia: final note on cost: if we adopt burst autoscaling and route to hosted fallback, cost of promotions likely shifts from on-prem reserved GPUs to on-demand hosted tokens — need product/finance input on tradeoffs.

sam: thanks team. I'll draft the postmortem and include timeline, root cause, mitigations, and follow-ups. Please update the tracking board with PR links. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy DPL-2026 (kernel tunables) was rolled back at 12:02 UTC as a precaution.

mira: added neteng, billing, and product to the PM board. Closing notes collected.
